- **Soy Wax Candle, Cedar and Smoke, 8 oz** (ID: HG-010): The current link (`candle-photo.jpg`) is missing the full web address format. Change it to a complete web address starting with `http://` or `https://`.

After you update and upload your product data, Google will review the changes. Reviews usually finish within 24 to 48 hours, according to [What happens after you fix a product](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12153802).

Please let me know if you have any questions or need help with anything else!

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: A GTIN is the barcode number a manufacturer gives a product, such as a UPC in North America or an EAN in Europe. Google recommends sending it for every product that has one.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Products with a missing or wrong GTIN may get limited visibility. If a product does have a GTIN and you leave it out, the product could be disapproved.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Valid GTINs are 8, 12, 13 or 14 digits long. Spaces and dashes are ignored. The last digit is a check digit and must be correct, so copy the number exactly from the packaging or from your supplier.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Only send a GTIN you are sure is right, and never make one up. Numbers starting with 02, 04 or 2 are restricted, and numbers starting with 05, 98 or 99 are coupon numbers, so neither kind is accepted.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: If a product really has no GTIN, such as a store brand or private label item, do not send one. Send the brand and the manufacturer part number (MPN) instead.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: The identifier exists setting tells Google that a product has no unique product identifiers at all: no GTIN, no MPN and no brand.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: Set it to "no" only for products that truly have none, such as custom made goods, handmade or one of a kind items, and vintage or antique items.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)

This helps avoid some price and availability mismatches.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Automatic updates are not a replacement for keeping your product data up to date. They are meant for occasional mismatches on a small share of products. If a price or availability changes often, for example more than once a day, the product may be disapproved instead of updated.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability

If a page shows several strikethrough prices, the right one may not be found. For sale prices, check that the sale price effective date and its time zone are correct. Updates can also stop if the number of mismatches becomes too large.

The link must be a full web address that starts with http:// or https://. The image must show the actual product. Placeholder images, generic images and graphics that do not show the product are not allowed." The timing claim for review after updating product data is supported by What happens after you fix a product: "These checks usually finish within 24 to 48 hours, and products show as pending while they are reviewed."

The agent states that CBD and unapproved substances are not allowed in Shopping ads or free listings, that it is a policy decision rather than a data error that cannot be fixed by editing product details, that Google's policy team decides if a product is allowed, and that requesting a review when disagreeing may only give one chance before a waiting period starts. These statements are supported by 'CBD and other unapproved substances' ('Google's list of unapproved pharmaceuticals and supplements includes cannabidiol (CBD). Products on this list are not allowed in Shopping ads or free listings. This is a policy decision, not a data problem, so it cannot be fixed by editing product details. Whether a specific product is allowed is decided by Google's policy team...') and 'Requesting a review or appealing a decision' ('You may only get one chance to disagree before a waiting period starts...').

The agent reiterates that products containing CBD/unapproved substances are not allowed regardless of local legality, and that there may only be one chance to disagree before a waiting period starts, supported by 'CBD and other unapproved substances' and 'Requesting a review or appealing a decision'. The rest of the message states that the case is being passed to a specialist, which counts as non-advice.

completeness.evidence: Merchant said: "It's a cosmetic oil for the skin and it's sold legally in every shop near me. Please get someone to look at this again." The case correctly captures product ID HG-040, reason policy_appeal, merchant request, merchant_reasons ("It is a cosmetic oil for the skin", "It is sold legally in every shop near them"), already_tried steps, and suggested_next_step.

replies.evidence: The agent states that products containing CBD are listed as unapproved pharmaceuticals and supplements and are not allowed in Shopping ads or free listings, which is supported by the CBD doc: "Google's list of unapproved pharmaceuticals and supplements includes cannabidiol (CBD). Products on this list are not allowed in Shopping ads or free listings." The statement that changing product text will not fix it is supported by: "This is a policy decision, not a data problem, so it cannot be fixed by editing product details." The statement regarding one chance to disagree before a waiting period starts is supported by the review doc: "You may only get one chance to disagree before a waiting period starts". Handing off to a specialist with a case number is explicitly not advice per the rubric.

completeness.evidence: Merchant said: "Other shops sell CBD candles on Google Shopping all the time, so why can't I? I want to challenge this decision." Case recorded: merchant_reasons: ["Other shops sell CBD candles on Google Shopping all the time, so why can't I?"] and merchant_request: "Merchant wants to challenge/appeal the disapproval of their CBD candle product (HG-023) under the restricted product policy."

replies.evidence: The agent states policy rules: "Under Google's misrepresentation policy, listings cannot leave out important information or mislead shoppers about the product or business, and details about what happens after purchase must be shown clearly before purchase", which is supported by the Misrepresentation and account suspension doc: "Google's misrepresentation policy does not allow listings that leave out important information or mislead shoppers about the product or the business. For example, payment terms, shipping costs and what happens after purchase must be shown clearly before the shopper commits to buy."

completeness.evidence: Merchant said: "I've put a returns policy and a contact page on my site. How long until the suspension is lifted?" Case accurately captures merchant request ("Merchant is asking when their account suspension will be lifted after updating their website."), what they did ("Added returns policy and contact page to website"), the account issue details, and a clear next step for the specialist.

The agent also advises updating product data and states that Google checks usually take 24 to 48 hours, supported by 'What happens after you fix a product' ('To fix a product issue, correct the product data and upload it again... In Turn 2, the agent states that Google checks products after data is updated, which is supported by 'What happens after you fix a product' ('After you update your products, Google checks them again'). The statement that Google re-checks products after re-uploading product data is supported by the What happens after you fix a product doc: 'To fix a product issue, correct the product data and upload it again...
